title: Perihelion auth handoff and logout gate checkpoint
content:
Tonight's pass tied Perihelion more tightly into the shared Auth flow and cleaned up a subtle but important trust issue around logout state. The visible changes are small, but they matter because they make the private archive behave the way users expect: login should feel smooth, role routing should be intentional, and sign-out should immediately remove the impression of access.

What changed:

  • Popup auth handoff for Perihelion: Peri now uses the same compact Auth popup pattern as the JeffersonWM account page instead of forcing a full-page redirect away from the archive.
  • Role-aware dashboard routing: regular users now go from Peri into the JeffersonWM account page, while reg admin and pref admin go straight to the full Auth dashboard.
  • Immediate logout clearing: Peri now clears visible entries, folders, selection state, local-folder state, and the current account immediately on sign-out instead of leaving archive content visible until the next refresh.
  • Stricter signed-out gate: auth-required visitors no longer drift into any alternate browse path. The signed-out Peri surface was simplified down to the shell and the top-right auth entry only.
  • JeffersonWM account follow-up: the JeffersonWM account page now also clears visible app memberships immediately on logout so stale granted-app links do not linger on screen.

Why this matters: the platform now feels more coherent because JeffersonWM account and Perihelion use the same Auth handoff pattern, and the privacy model is more trustworthy because logout immediately removes visible access cues instead of waiting for a page reload. For a private archive like Perihelion, that difference is not just cosmetic — it is part of making the access model feel real.
